transit.name: Rocky Mountain National Park Hiker Shuttle
transit.detail: Estes Park Visitor Center to the park's Park & Ride on Bear Lake Road. In 2026: daily May 22–Sept. 7, weekends Sept. 12–Oct. 18. Reserve on Recreation.gov, $2 per reservation.

nameOrigin.text: The town is named for Joel Estes, the valley's first settler of European descent. William N. Byers of the Rocky Mountain News visited in August 1864 and was the first to call the valley Estes Park in print.

founded.text: Joel Estes found the valley in the fall of 1859 and started a ranch.

timeline.text: The road up the Big Thompson River, now Highway 34, was completed.
Rocky Mountain National Park was dedicated on September 4.
The Town of Estes Park was incorporated on April 17.

sites.name: The Stanley Hotel
sites.hours: 60-minute guided Historic Tours; advance reservations recommended
sites.cost: Historic Tour $30 per person; $20 ages 8-17; $28 hotel guests

sites.name: Stanley Home Museum
sites.hours: Guided tours at 10 am, 12 pm and 2 pm; Sundays at 12 pm and 2 pm; closed Mondays, with fewer open days outside summer
sites.cost: $25 adults; $15 seniors 65 and older, active military and veterans; free 8 and younger

sites.name: MacGregor Ranch Museum
sites.season: Summer; closed for the season as of November 2026

makers.name: The Taffy Shop
makers.what: Salt water taffy, made in the shop since 1935

places.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
places.what: The national park at the west edge of town, entered on US 36 at Beaver Meadows or on US 34 at Fall River. It is open 24 hours a day, all year, weather permitting.

facts.label: Entrance pass
facts.value: Needed 24 hours a day, all year, in every part of the park, Lily Lake and Lumpy Ridge included: $30 a vehicle for one day, $35 for seven, $70 for the park’s annual pass; under 16 free. Cards only at the gates.

facts.label: Non-US visitors
facts.value: $100 a person, 16 and older, on top of the entrance fee, unless admitted with an annual or America the Beautiful pass.

facts.label: Timed entry
facts.value: Not needed now. In 2026 it ran May 22 to October 12, 9 am–2 pm, and on Bear Lake Road to October 18, 5 am–6 pm, sold only on Recreation.gov. 2027 dates: not yet announced.

facts.label: Roads now
facts.value: Trail Ridge Road closed to through travel for the winter on November 13, 2026; Bear Lake Road is open all year, and the park’s shuttles return in summer 2027.

facts.label: Dogs
facts.value: Not on any trail, tundra or meadow, nor on the park’s buses; on a leash of 6 feet or less along roads and in parking areas, campgrounds and picnic areas.

places.name: Elk and the fall rut
places.what: Large elk herds spend autumn and winter in the park’s meadow valleys. The rut, their mating season, is in September and October.

facts.label: Where and when
facts.value: September and October, near meadows and where meadows meet forest; bulls bugle most at dawn and dusk.

facts.label: Rut closures
facts.value: September 1 to October 31, 5 pm to 10 am daily: no walking off roads and designated trails in Horseshoe Park, Moraine Park, Upper Beaver Meadows, Harbison Meadow and Holzwarth Meadow.

facts.label: Distance
facts.value: Stay at least 75 feet away, about two bus lengths. Calling elk and using lights to spot them are illegal.

facts.label: Elk Fest
facts.value: October 2 and 3, 2027, in Bond Park; free.

places.name: The Stanley Hotel
places.what: The hotel on Wonderview Avenue north of downtown, open to visitors who are not staying, for tours, meals and shows.

facts.label: Where
facts.value: 333 E. Wonderview Ave.

facts.label: Tours
facts.value: The 60-minute Historic Tour is $30, $20 for ages 8 to 17, and not open to children under 8; the ghost and Shining tours are $35, ages 8 and up. 2027 tours are on sale, and the hotel recommends booking ahead.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: $10 a vehicle for day visitors.

facts.label: Dogs
facts.value: Only trained service animals in the buildings.

places.name: Downtown and the Riverwalk
places.what: Downtown is Elkhorn Avenue, the Riverwalk and Bond Park, the Town’s green in front of Town Hall at 170 MacGregor Avenue.

facts.label: Parking
facts.value: The Town’s free structure at 691 North St. Vrain Avenue, by the Visitor Center: 415 spaces on four levels. Downtown lots were paid May 22 to October 18 in 2026 and are free until late May.

facts.label: On foot
facts.value: Under ten minutes from the structure, the Town says: over the footbridge across the Big Thompson River and through the lighted tunnel under US 36 to the Riverwalk.

facts.label: Bond Park
facts.value: 46,000 square feet of lawn with picnic tables and benches, where the downtown festivals, concerts and art fairs are held.

facts.label: Town shuttle
facts.value: The Peak, the Town’s free buses, runs from late May to late October.

places.name: Lake Estes
places.what: The lake by the Visitor Center, ringed by a paved trail, with a marina run by the Estes Valley Recreation and Park District.

facts.label: Trail
facts.value: A paved 4-mile loop, rated easy; dogs welcome on a leash. Join it from the Visitor Center, parking-garage or Fisherman’s Nook lots, or the paid lots at Cherokee Draw, Wapiti Meadows and the marina; restrooms at Cherokee Draw.

facts.label: Paid lots
facts.value: $8 a vehicle for the day at the marina, Wapiti Meadows and Cherokee Draw.

facts.label: Marina
facts.value: 1770 Big Thompson Ave., 970-586-2011: closed for the season until spring 2027.

facts.label: Rules
facts.value: A Colorado fishing license for anyone 16 and older. No swimming, jet skis, water skiing or ice fishing.

trails.name: Bear Lake Loop
trails.length: 0.6 mile, a loop, with 71 feet of climbing
trails.trailhead: Bear Lake Trailhead, at the end of Bear Lake Road, 9.2 miles from Trail Ridge Road, at 9,475 feet. The lot is often full by 9 am, all year.
trails.season: All year, weather permitting; Bear Lake Road stays open in winter. Expect snow-packed trails from October to early June.
trails.dogs: Not allowed on any park trail.
trails.fee: A park entrance pass ($30 a vehicle for a day). In the timed-entry season, a Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road reservation; in 2026, 5 am–6 pm from May 22 to October 18.

trails.name: Sprague Lake Loop
trails.length: 0.8 mile, a flat loop that is wheelchair and stroller accessible (0.7 mile on the park’s Sprague Lake page)
trails.trailhead: Sprague Lake Parking Area on Bear Lake Road, with 27 picnic tables and a vault toilet open all year
trails.season: Open all year; ice fishing in winter.
trails.dogs: Not allowed on the trail; on a leash in the parking and picnic areas.
trails.fee: A park entrance pass ($30 a vehicle for a day). In the timed-entry season, a Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road reservation; in 2026, 5 am–6 pm from May 22 to October 18.

trails.name: Hermit Park Open Space
trails.address: On US 36 about 4 miles southeast of downtown Estes Park; the entrance is on the right heading out of town
trails.season: March 1 to December 20; closed for winter from December 21 to the end of February.
trails.dogs: On a leash no longer than 10 feet, and never left alone.
trails.fee: An entrance permit for every visit, on foot or by bike too; $10 a vehicle for the day.
